sourceNote: Transcribed from Workout.pdf. Many exercise descriptions were truncated in the source (the underlying PDF text layer itself cuts off, not just the visual rendering -- confirmed via pdftotext). Lines with needsReview:true and a reviewNote were completed by Claude with a reasonable assumption and MUST be spot-checked against your own memory of the program before you trust them mid-workout. Lines with only prescriptionComplete:false and no reviewNote are still literally cut off with no safe assumption made (rep count unknown).

logModes.cumulative: Tap-add chunks of reps until repTarget is reached (rest-pause / century sets).

blockTypes.superset: Two exercises back to back, no rest between.
blockTypes.triSet: Three movements performed continuously as one set.
blockTypes.giantSet: Four or more movements performed continuously as one set.
blockTypes.dropSet: Weight reduced dropsPerSet times within a single set.
blockTypes.restPause: Single set taken past failure with short pauses until repTarget. Also used for 'century sets' (push-to-100 single sets) -- see open item below.

openItems: Legs, week 1: day header says 'Giant Set #1 - Quads (3 Rounds/Sets)' but Leg Extensions underneath specifies 6 individual sets with a 50-100 rep ramp. Contradiction, not resolved -- flagged needsReview on w1-legs.

Shoulders, week 1: 'Machine Rear Delt SS Seated Dumbbell Side Lateral' block appears twice consecutively (w1-sh-b6, w1-sh-b7) -- confirm intentional double volume vs. copy-paste duplication in the source.
Chest+Abs, week 2: no Abs block present in the source for this day, unlike every other Chest+Abs day in the program -- confirm this is intentional.

'Century sets' (T-Bar Row, DB Shrug, week 4 Back+Traps) don't have a dedicated block type in the current 6-type enum -- mapped to restPause + logMode cumulative as the closest fit. Consider adding a 7th block type (e.g. centurySet) if you want it visually distinct in the UI.

A number of week 3/4/bonus lines have rep counts genuinely missing from the source (not just an assumed word, the number itself) -- these are left as repScheme: null / 'reps not specified in source' rather than guessed, since guessing a number felt too unreliable. Search for these in the reviewNotes.
